sentences.text: This petition has been filed for quashing of FIR No.146/2007 under sections 498A/406/34 IPC at PS Krishna Nagar on the basis of settlement arrived at between the parties 2.
Petitioner nos. 1 and 2 and respondent nos. 1 to 6 are all present in the Court and have been duly identified by the IO and the counsel.
3. Petitioner no.1 is the husband of respondent no.2.

Respondent no.2, due to an accident in 2015,
has since been comatose and in persisting vegetative stage with 100 % disability since 2016.

As a result, the father of respondent No.2 Sh. Gulshan Bhatia (who is present in the Court) filed a writ petition W.P.(Crl.) 4697/2019 before this Court for appointing him as guardian of his daughter,
respondent no.2 which was allowed vide order dated 9th December, 2019 and Sh. Gulshan Bhatia was appointed as guardian of respondent no.2 for all the purposes.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 21:46:46 4.
One male child born out of wedlock between petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2, is under the custody of Sh. Gulshan Bhatia.
As a result of matrimonial disputes, earlier, the said FIR had been registered.

The issues have now been settled before the Mediation Centre, Karkardooma Courts on Shri Rahul Bhatia & Anr vs State Of Nct Of Delhi & Anr on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58373420/
1 14th January, 2021 and it has been noted in the said settlement that Sh. Gulshan Bhatia has entered into settlement as guardian of respondent no.2.

entities.text: Shri Rahul Bhatia & Anr vs State Of Nct Of Delhi & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, as per the said settlement, total amount of Rs.9 lacs had to be paid which has now been fully received by Sh. Gulshan Bhatia on behalf of respondent no.2.
Sh. Gulshan Bhatia acknowledges the same and states that he has no objection to the quashing of the FIR.
No further compliances are stated to be pending under the said settlement.

5. The divorce proceedings between petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 were also pursued by Sh.
Gulshan Bhatia on behalf of respondent no.2.
6.

Considering the above settlement between the parties and the chances of conviction of the petitioners being remote and bleak, there is no use continuing with proceedings of the present FIR as it would be a misuse of the process of the Court and an unnecessary burden on the State exchequer.
Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Consequently, the FIR No.146/2007 under sections 498A/406/34 IPC at PS Krishna Nagar and proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
It is however made clear that the said settlement will not affect the rights of the minor child in future.
7. Parties shall abide by the terms of settlement.
8. Accordingly, the petition is disposed of.
Pending applications (if any) are disposed of as infructuous.
9. Order be uploaded on the website of this Court.
ANISH DAYAL, J MAY 22, 2023/sm
